segments.text: Welcome to the Robotics News Digest for November 14, 2026.
Today we cover the drone revolution, major investment in drone manufacturing, and exciting advancements in human motion for robots.
From Robotics & Automation News, Wing invests $125 million in US drone manufacturing to support nationwide expansion.
This report details Wing's significant investment in domestic drone production aimed at scaling nationwide delivery services.

Wing has committed up to one hundred twenty-five million dollars over two years for this manufacturing effort, which includes the construction of a new fifteen thousand square foot facility in Fort Worth, Texas, projected to create up to one hundred jobs.

This expansion is designed to facilitate the extension of drone delivery services to more than forty million Americans across nearly twenty United States markets by the year two thousand twenty seven.

The company has already finalized over one million residential deliveries within the United States this year, positioning this manufacturing growth to support the expansion of autonomous aerial delivery systems amidst developing United States aviation regulations.
This development signals increased industrial focus on drone infrastructure within the technology sector.
From Robotics & Automation News, Zipline raises an unbelievable $1.5 billion to build nationwide drone delivery network.
This report details the company's effort to expand its nationwide drone delivery system through significant capital investment.
Zipline secured one point five billion dollars to expand its drone delivery network, intending to overcome limitations associated with ground delivery methods.
This capital is designated to fund the expansion of United States manufacturing and hiring necessary to construct the system.
Growth is being facilitated through partnerships with entities such as Walmart and Uber, with a stated objective of reaching one million deliveries per day by the year 2029.
The service is recognized for its speed, convenience, and reduced traffic impact, supported by rapid delivery times.

The company is concurrently focusing on technological advancement, incorporating improvements to aircraft efficiency and operation, and maintains a successful record in autonomous delivery operations.
This development signals continued investment in autonomous logistics infrastructure and technological deployment across the sector.
From NVIDIA Developer Blog, "Adapt Human Motion for Robots with NVIDIA SOMA Retargeter".
This report details the development of a system that adapts human motion data for humanoid robots utilizing the shared SOMA skeleton representation.
The system scales motion targets, resolves inverse kinematics through NVIDIA Warp, and incorporates post-processing such as foot-plant adjustment to align with robot proportions.
Developers can source motion from diverse datasets or generative models to export retargeted trajectories for policy training workflows.
Tools like the Robot Configurator facilitate the refinement of robot configurations and the optimization of inverse-kinematics priorities for smoother motion.
This mechanism enables the adaptation of human movement to teach humanoid robots locomotion and for simulation evaluation.
This advancement facilitates the training of sophisticated humanoid robotics systems through realistic motion transfer.
From Robotics & Automation News, "Why Build a Humanoid Robot From the Sensor Up? The Thinking Behind GENTO’s CoRL 2026 Debut"
reports on the development philosophy behind GENTO's humanoid robot systems, which centers on incorporating MEMS torque sensors within each joint to dictate robot reactions to contact.
Tianji Intelligence developed a five-tier system encompassing sensors, integrated joint modules, dual arms, whole-body systems, and a dexterous hand.
This system employs high-sensitivity sensors capable of measuring torque as low as 0.02 Newton-meters to achieve accurate force control.

This methodology enabled demonstrations on platforms such as the TIANJI Marvin Pro system utilized in NVIDIA's GR00T open-world action model, emphasizing the goal of achieving gentle interaction through precise joint torque readings.
This approach signals a focus on fine-grained physical interaction in future robotics development.
From The Robot Report, "Six AGIBOT G2 Robots Complete 1,730 Tasks in 24-Hour Shanghai Convenience Store Trial".
This report details the successful completion of a 24-hour trial where six AGIBOT G2 robots executed one thousand seven hundred thirty tasks within a Shanghai convenience store setting.

The trial assessed the efficacy of embodied artificial intelligence in navigating a dynamic retail environment, demonstrating the robots' capacity to perform customer assistance and restocking duties.
The operation relied on the robots utilizing real-time visual information to adjust to shifting conditions, enabling actions such as repositioning merchandise and managing liquid spills.
The Genie Master framework managed the coordinated activities, facilitating the learning process from operational experiences to refine subsequent performance.
AGIBOT intends to proceed with further real-world testing to further improve the dependability and adaptability of these robotic systems.
This development indicates progress in applying embodied AI to complex, real-world retail automation.
From Robotics & Automation News, "Automated Warehouses: Why Safety Infrastructure Matters More Than Ever".
This story examines the necessity of robust safety infrastructure in increasingly automated warehouse environments to manage risks from moving machinery and personnel.
Effective safety measures are crucial for preventing collisions and ensuring smooth operations in this complex setting.
The implementation of effective safety measures requires clearly defined traffic routes and floor markings to delineate paths for pedestrians and automated vehicles.
Furthermore, warehouse flooring must possess the capacity to endure heavy traffic and incorporate slip-resistant finishes to mitigate potential hazards.
Comprehensive safety necessitates an integration of intelligent technology and physical protection, supported by routine safety assessments.
This focus on integrated physical and technological safety protocols indicates a growing mandate for safety-by-design principles across the industrial automation sector.
From Robotics & Automation News, Neura Robotics partners with E.ON to bring humanoid robots to energy infrastructure.
This collaboration involves the development of physical artificial intelligence applications for electricity networks through intelligent robots.
Neura Robotics, E.ON, and enviaM are collaborating on this project to deploy robots for inspecting and monitoring energy infrastructure and assisting personnel with physically demanding tasks.
Training for these robotic systems will take place at a specialized facility utilizing multimodal artificial intelligence and real-world data to cultivate robotic skills.
A prospective application involves employing humanoid robots to traverse existing infrastructure for inspection and maintenance support.
Initial practical trials are slated to commence in 2027 with Mitnetz Strom serving as the pilot partner.
This development signals a progression in applying advanced robotics to complex utility environments.
From Robotics & Automation News, Gecko Robotics unveils faster Raptor inspection robot, with ADNOC as first customer.
This report details the introduction of the Raptor, a next-generation industrial inspection robot capable of collecting data on critical infrastructure significantly faster than current models.
The Raptor features improved mobility enabling navigation through complex spaces and the ability to execute three-point turns while inspecting pipelines and tanks.
The robot is designed to gather millions of data points, which are subsequently analyzed using Gecko's proprietary artificial intelligence software.
ADNOC in the United Arab Emirates is the initial customer for the Raptor, and plans are underway for further international installations.
This development signals advancements in autonomous industrial inspection technology and the integration of advanced AI in remote data acquisition.
From IEEE Spectrum - Robotics, Video Friday: NASA PROMISEs a New Moon Rover.

This report details NASA's plan to send a nuclear-powered rover named PROMISE to the Moon's South Pole as a key mission for the Moon Base Program, leveraging components from Mars rovers Curiosity and Perseverance.
A demonstration of automated in-space assembly was achieved when a Caltech payload successfully built a truss structure in orbit.
Various robotics applications are being explored, including the use of mobile robots for security and solving complex multi-agent planning problems in manufacturing.
Further developments are occurring across areas including humanoid robotics, autonomous navigation, and artificial intelligence in motion.
This work indicates progression in autonomous systems and advanced hardware development.
From Robotics & Automation News, Queue introduces robotic pharmacy kiosk that fills prescriptions in 30 seconds.
This report details the unveiling of an autonomous robotic pharmacy kiosk designed to fill, verify, and label prescriptions in approximately thirty seconds.

The system is engineered to manage three hundred forty medications through machine vision for verification, and installation can be completed in less than a day without requiring patient membership fees.

The process involves a patient pickup code initiating automated medication preparation and software handling insurance and payment, targeting community pharmacies, retail chains, and clinics to dispense medications without a traditional storefront.
This technology seeks to improve medication access and mitigate pharmacy closures by addressing healthcare access disparities.
The advancement signifies a tangible application of automation in the pharmaceutical sector.
From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, AIRoA-0!".
This segment reports on the AIRoA-0 robot foundation model and its foundation in Japanese AI research.
The key finding is the model's focus on connecting AI research with robot control through an alternative data collection method.
The AIRoA-0 model originates from Japan's AI Robot Association and received support from the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry.
It falls into the vision-language action model category, emphasizing the connection between artificial intelligence research and robot control.
The model was trained using more than sixteen thousand hours of human recordings gathered via YUBI, a handheld gripper developed by Toyota.
This project prioritizes an alternative method for building robot training datasets that minimizes the necessity for extensive robot operation.
The research focus is placed on demonstration collection costs and open distribution.
This development points toward new approaches for efficient robot training data generation in the wider technology sector.
From Humanoid.guide, "ASUS Gallop humanoid learns to pack motherboard accessories".

This story details the training of the Gallop humanoid to perform the task of packing motherboard accessories in a group electronics manufacturing services factory, achieving a ninety-nine point five percent task success rate within twenty seconds.
The training process involved worker demonstrations, simulation, and practical practice using the actual components.
The humanoid handled fifteen varied accessories, which utilized small, thin, and flexible plastic packaging materials.
This was accomplished through iterative learning methodologies within the factory setting.
ASUS plans for commercial availability in the second half of twenty twenty-eight, succeeding prior customer pilot programs in twenty twenty-seven.
This development signals advancements in dexterous manipulation for robotic systems in manufacturing environments.
From Humanoid.guide, Apple HALO reaches reported 91% success on Unitree G1 tests.

This report details an evaluation of the Apple HALO humanoid control system demonstrating a ninety-one percent success rate across three hundred sixty single-task trials conducted on a Unitree G1 in six different, unseen real environments.
The testing involved thirty hundred hours of simulated motion across virtual rooms featuring randomized visual variations to facilitate training.

The system operates through a three-level architecture where a task interpreter generates movement instructions which are subsequently executed by a motion-tracking layer, with the research aiming to assess the transfer of synthetic experience to unfamiliar physical spaces.
This finding indicates progress in enabling artificial general intelligence to operate effectively in unpredictable physical settings.
From The Robot Report, Narwal builds robot vacuums to serve regional needs.
This report details Narwal's development of robot vacuums and mops through a user-centered innovation approach that addresses specific household pain points.
The company pioneered features such as carpet deep-cleaning and a tangle-free system, focusing on solving real-world user issues rather than incremental hardware stacking.
Narwal maintains control over its technology and supply chain by building these systems in-house within China, facilitating rapid iteration.

The company employs an experience-first strategy, aiming for these devices to meet established household appliance standards, with future development concentrating on embodied intelligence to advance robots into full-space housekeepers.
This development signals a shift toward functionally focused robotics in the consumer goods sector.
From Robotics & Automation News, ABB Robotics brings industrial-grade physical AI to fashion logistics.

This report details the launch of an end-to-end vision-based physical AI solution integrating the AI Robot Trainer into the Fashion Inductor module, which facilitates the deployment and optimization of AI-powered fashion logistics applications with reduced effort and risk.
The Fashion Inductor already utilizes AI-powered path planning and vision technology to achieve high sorting performance in logistics environments.
The AI Robot Trainer component significantly reduces engineering and commissioning effort by up to seventy-five percent through the provision of pre-trained models and rapid retraining capabilities.
This system incorporates a digital twin and a closed-loop workflow designed for continuous performance improvement throughout the entire system lifecycle.
This development signals a step toward deploying complex physical AI solutions directly into high-demand logistics sectors.
From Robotics & Automation News, Expoline completes international logistics project for humanoid robots.
This report details the successful multimodal logistics operation managed by the South Korean specialist for a global physical AI robotics company.

Expoline managed the transportation of sensitive robotic equipment from China to South Korea for the 2026 Seoul AI Robot Show, handling customs clearance, exhibition booth delivery, and the safe return shipment to China through an air import and ocean return strategy.
The operation involved specialized handling and adherence to ATA Carnet regulations without customs delays.
This successful execution underscores Expoline's expertise in advanced robotics logistics and international exhibition support.
The demonstrated capability points toward increased reliance on specialized logistical support for the growing physical AI robotics sector.

From Robotics & Automation News, NEXCOM expands the RoboWIZ robotics platform with new technology partners, establishing an open ecosystem to simplify the integration of advanced technologies into robotic systems.
The expansion involves partnerships with technology providers including RealSense, Stereolabs, Synapticon, and Reynolds & Moore.
The RoboWIZ platform functions by creating an open system that permits developers to combine components from diverse suppliers rather than limiting them to a single hardware architecture.
This modular approach encompasses five core areas: AI core control, functional safety, visual perception, real-time control, and actuation.
This methodology is designed to reduce the complexity associated with developing and integrating these technologies for various robot applications.
This development signals a push toward more flexible and accessible integration methods within the robotics and artificial intelligence sectors.
From Robotics & Automation News, Humble Robotics raises fifty-one million dollars to expand autonomous electric freight operations.

The company secured this Series A funding, bringing its total funding to seventy-five million dollars, to advance autonomous electric freight operations through a unified platform for seamless dock-to-dock transport.

Humble Robotics focuses on developing an autonomous, electric platform designed to facilitate transport between various logistics points, currently concentrating efforts on regional freight routes under two hundred fifty miles.

This new capital will be allocated to customer pilots, testing procedures, and the expansion of the company's modular vehicle platform, with the stated goal of enhancing the safety, reliability, and scalability of autonomous freight.
This development signals further investment in the commercial application and expansion of autonomous logistics technology within the transportation sector.
From The Robot Report, "How Rhoda AI is using video data to create generalized AI models for robots".
This report details how Rhoda AI pretrains models on internet-scale video to build a strong understanding of motion, physics, and physical interaction essential for robotics.

The company's Direct Video Action model incorporates video history and language tokens to predict subsequent video frames and translate those predictions into executable robot actions through a cycle of observation, prediction, action execution, and a new observation loop for continuous learning.

This generalized approach leverages broad video data to enable models to generalize across various robot forms before fine-tuning with task-specific data for practical applications in manufacturing and logistics.
The development indicates a pathway toward more adaptable and capable robotic systems across industrial settings.
And that’s all the circuits for today!
Wing is really taking flight with that drone investment.
Thanks for powering up your day with us.
Until tomorrow, keep building amazing things!
